messages:
sasha: quick heads-up — pushed mb_size=8 on the streaming-chat canary this morning and p99 jumped to ~2.1s (baseline ~1.2s). non-streaming completions on same machine stayed healthy. looks like kernel fallback + KV churn.
perf-bot: profile summary for canary xyz: 6/20 traces show kernel fallback, median extra latency ~800ms, KV cache miss rate 42% on first 5 tokens, heavy tail after handshake.
perf-bot: trace snippet:\n```\n[2026-03-17T13:10:22Z] trace=xyz request=abc model=gpt-open-8k seq_len=64 mb_size=8 kernel_hint=fast_attn -> fallback=matmul_lowp (reason=kernel_selector:runtime_overload)\nkv_cache: miss_rate=0.42 prefetch=off \nworker_latency_ms: base=120 extra_fallback=780 total=900\n```\nraj: hmm. mb_size=8 increases kernel selection pressure; fallback suggests a kernel with worse throughput for short responses. streaming has many short-turn tokens so fallback kills tail. suggest: drop stream mb_size->4 and keep completions at 8.
elaine: +1. we saw similar on staging when kv warmup lagged. adding a tiny client_hold (50ms) reduced the tail because it let prefix batching finish and warmed KV.
mike: can we instead change kernel hinting heuristic? force fast_attn for seq<=128 and prefer it unless sustained >tput threshold. that would avoid matmul fallback for short chats.
ivy: proposed quick experiment plan:\n1) revert streaming pool to mb_size=4 (immediate)\n2) enable kv-prefetch for new handshakes for 10s\n3) add kernel-pref hint: prefer fast_attn for seq<=128 (soft)\n4) instrument tracepoints and run 30m canary\nI can run steps 1+2 now.
sasha: thanks @ivy — doing step1 now. will patch runtime flags for pool-streaming -> mb=4 and roll canary.
raj: also consider adding per-client burst queue depth limit. when some clients burst, they force large merged batches that flip kernel selection.
elaine: FYI, last month we had a regression where a kernel binary got evicted under memory pressure; check node-level OOM churn in the same window.
perf-bot: note: runtime-r123 included a kernel-selector hysteresis change (backoff_ms -> 0 -> 100ms). if canary used older runtime, mismatch might surface as fallback flapping.
mike: if fallback flaps, p99 will look noisy; hysteresis fix could help. but smaller mb_size + kv-prefetch is lowest-risk rollback.
sasha: canary update: after mb_size->4 p99 dropped ~40% over 15m; p95 roughly unchanged. posting graphs in #eng-runtime-dash in a minute.
ivy: running kv-prefetch toggle next. will follow up with perf-bot traces.
raj: if we confirm, follow-up task: add explicit routing rule so stream chat pools default to small-mb kernels and completions to bulk kernels. reduces cross-workload interference.
sasha: filing follow-up ticket after canary: ENGRT-1428. thanks all :thumbsup:
perf-bot: automated note: attach traces with tag engruntime/canary/3776543210 for later triage.
